title: Section 321 De Minimis in 2026: What US Importers Need to Know
summary: Understand Section 321 de minimis changes in 2026, compare postal and non-postal entry routes, and see what low-value imports mean for your customs budget.
body_markdown:
[Hero photo: medino marketing / Unsplash. Illustrative packaged merchandise.](https://unsplash.com/photos/medino-cardboard-boxes-nXhND4y3riM)


A small parcel can carry a substantial customs bill. The familiar **Section 321** exemption for low-value imports is suspended, so an order below $800 does not automatically enter the US duty-free.


This guide covers commercial merchandise and the current postal and non-postal routes. Separate provisions for qualifying gifts and travelers' articles have their own conditions.


## What Section 321 used to allow


The **Section 321 de minimis** provision commonly used for ecommerce covered qualifying merchandise imported by one person on one day, within a $800 limit. The valuation and anti-splitting conditions appear in[19 CFR 10.151](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-19/chapter-I/part-10/section-10.151) .


That historical threshold remains visible in older guidance. Its presence does not establish present eligibility.


**By the numbers**


[$800 Historical de minimis limit Exemption now suspended](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USDHSCBP/bulletins/41fa7f0)[$2,500 General postal informal limit Eligibility conditions apply](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USDHSCBP/bulletins/41fa7f0)


Source: CBP, July 2026 postal guidance. The informal-entry limit is not a duty-free allowance.


## Where the rules stand in October 2026


### Non-postal shipments


CBP's[non-postal regulation](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-06-24/pdf/2026-12670.pdf) indefinitely suspends the exemption. Commercial courier, air-cargo, ocean, and land shipments need an appropriate entry route and assessment of applicable duties and charges.


### International mail


The postal exemption is also suspended under[19 CFR 145.31](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-19/section-145.31) . CBP introduced a new[postal informal entry process](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USDHSCBP/bulletins/41fa7f0) in July 2026, generally for qualifying mailed merchandise valued at $2,500 or less. Informal entry still involves customs requirements and applicable duties.


## Which entry route applies?


### Courier or freight


An old **Section 321 entry** workflow needs reassessment. A broker or qualified filer determines the applicable formal or informal entry, considering value, product restrictions, and agency requirements. The[US customs clearance guide](https://www.dripcapital.com/en-us/resources/blog/us-customs-clearance-process) explains the broader process.


### Postal informal entry


Under[CBP's postal guidance](https://content.govdelivery.com/attachments/USDHSCBP/2026/07/08/file_attachments/3708650/Updated%20Global%20Guidance%20for%20International%20Mail-7.7.26.pdf) , eligible filers must arrange the required bond, submit shipment data, and pay duties. Data include origin, value, and applicable 10-digit HTS classifications. The standard postal process has reporting and payment deadlines on the seventh day of the following month.


### Electronic mail entries and exceptions


CBP's voluntary[Entry Type 13 test](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-06-24/pdf/2026-12668.pdf) ,[implemented in September 2026](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USDHSCBP/bulletins/42d494a) , provides an electronic ACE route for qualifying mail, including certain goods outside the standard postal process. Antidumping/countervailing-duty and quota shipments remain excluded from the test.


CBP has[extended the compliance deadline](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-10-22/html/2026-21600.htm) for 19 CFR 145.12(a)(2)(v) and (vi) from October 22, 2026 to January 20, 2027. The extension covers international postal shipments subject to Partner Government Agency requirements, Chapter 98/99 duties, or claims for duty-free treatment under Chapter 98 or a free trade agreement. From January 20, 2027, affected shipments require formal entry or, where eligible, the Entry Type 13 test. The extension does not restore the $800 de minimis exemption. Confirm shipment-specific treatment with the filer.


Separately, CBP[temporarily permits Entry Type 13 filings without complete electronic Partner Government Agency data](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-10-22/html/2026-21570.htm) . The end of this transition will be announced in a future Federal Register notice; January 20, 2027 is not its announced end date.


## How costs change


There is no universal replacement **Section 321** tariff rate. Product classification, origin, customs value, and applicable trade measures determine the assessment. A zero ordinary tariff rate can still require review of additional duties and charges.


For illustration, assume a parcel has a $500 customs value and an applicable 10% duty. Duty is **$50** . Add any applicable entry, brokerage, bond, transport, or handling costs separately; these assumptions are not a tariff quote.

## What belongs in the shipment file?


### Product and origin


Use a specific description, accurate value, and substantiated country of origin. Match the[commercial invoice](https://www.dripcapital.com/en-us/resources/blog/commercial-invoice-what-it-is-what-goes-in-it) to the actual goods and transaction.


### Quantities and delivery terms


Reconcile quantities against the[packing list](https://www.dripcapital.com/en-us/resources/blog/export-packing-list) . Record who handles clearance and pays charges, alongside tracking and entry records.


### Cash timing


Put vendor payments, customs costs, and expected sales receipts into the same forecast. Small parcel size does not remove the funding gap between those dates.

## Frequently asked questions


### Is the $800 exemption available for commercial imports?


The exemption commonly called **Section 321 de minimis** is currently suspended for postal and non-postal merchandise. Review the current entry requirements even when a parcel is below $800.


### Does every small parcel require formal entry?


Some shipments qualify for an informal process. Value, commodity restrictions, and the available filing route determine eligibility.


### Can splitting an order restore duty-free treatment?


Splitting an order does not restore the suspended exemption. The historical rule also restricted deliberate splitting to secure free entry or avoid applicable requirements.


### Is there one tariff rate for all low-value shipments?


No single rate applies to all products and origins. Classification, valuation, trade measures, and any valid preferential claim must be assessed for the shipment.
